newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka leader gets MPs support on devolution.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka leader gets MPs support on devolution.

text.p: Lawmakers from Sri Lanka's ruling People's Alliance coalition have given their backing to President Chandrika Kumaratunga's proposed constitutional reforms aimed at ending a protracted ethnic war.
Alliance parliamentary deputies met at a resort south of the capital Colombo this week to discuss a devolution package, among other proposals.

An alliance statement on Wednesday said the lawmkers also supported the president's proposal that the offensive against the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) should continue parallel to the implementation of the devolution proposals.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed since the war began in 1983.

"PA parliamentarians...unanimously endorsed the draft constitution for Sri Lanka, which seeks to devolve part of the authority of the central government as the basis of a solution to the complex ethnic issue, while vigorously prosecuting the war against the LTTE with the firm determination of securing victory," the statement said.

The new constitution is being debated in a parliamentary select committee, but the process has slowed down due to disagreements between Tamil and Moslem parties, and between the main opposition United National Party (UNP) and the government.

The committee is negotiating key issues such as devolution of power to minorities and demarcation of proposed new councils in Sri Lanka's north and east, the LTTE's would-be homeland for minority Tamils.

Party sources said Kumaratunga also discussed the possibility of a possible national referendum on the constitution if the government felt it could not get the proposals through parliament with the necessary two-thirds majority.
A government minister told Reuters last week the UNP was unlikely to support the government over the new constitution in parliament, where the alliance has a one-seat majority.
Most Tamil parties, which support the alliance, have complained over the delay in implementation of the reforms and have said further delay might lead to an intensification of the ethnic war.
The select committee has been meeting for more than a year.
